findings.summary: The new base-pin admission/lifetime safety rule has no independent model assertion or caught mutation.
findings.evidence: spec.md S9 (lines67-70) requires the pinned base to remain retained until completion or deletion; S10 (lines72-75) requires every new safety rule to have a caught mutation. design.md:100-104 introduces a durable pin before Hydrating exposure and permits release only after Complete/deletion commits. However its concrete independent checks at :139-144 cover initial-value linearizability, acknowledged state agreement and post-Complete repository events; the nine named mutations do not omit initial pin acquisition or release a pin early. In the explicitly grow-only/no-GC repository, removing a pin need not change any data, read result, presence state or post-Complete fetch event, so all of those oracles can still pass while S9 is violated. The existing simulator check path (sim/mod.rs:1345-1407 and sim/check.rs:32-61) has no repository/pin oracle to supply this implicitly. The mapped #52 design similarly treats its own reader-pin closure as an independent checker and catches premature_pin_release; that is a distinct grant/source lifecycle and does not establish #68 destination-base pin coverage.
findings.fix: Define the modeled base-pin state and an independent per-transition assertion relating the immutable requested destination-incarnation/base identity to pin admission and terminal commits: no Hydrating exposure without its exact live pin, and no pin release before that incarnation’s Complete or deletion commit. Add deterministic/seeded cases for crash/retry, failed/lost completion and deletion/recreation, with at least omit-initial-pin and early-release mutations that each fail that assertion on a clean-passing scenario. Keep this in the protocol/model increment; no runtime repository collector, credential protocol, bucket mutation or wire-format implementation is required.
